_comment: Deck plan for scaffold_deck.py.
deck_type is REQUIRED and is not cosmetic: it decides the deck's length,
depth and tone. Establish it with the user BEFORE writing any slides
(SKILL.md STEP 0):
overview   recruiters / hiring managers -> short, outcome-first,
five or six content slides, little code.
deep-dive  engineers / technical interview -> architecture,
decisions and trade-offs, code where it explains something.
talk       meetup or team talk -> story-led: the problem, false
starts, the fix, the lessons.
Record the audience too, so the next update does not have to re-ask.
`deck_facts.py --deck-type <type>` prints the agenda skeleton these
phases should follow.
The phases[] order IS the slide order. Slide 0 is the title, slide 1 the
agenda, so the first content slide is index 2. The scaffolder computes
every agenda card's data-slide-target from that, which is the part that
silently breaks when slides are added by hand.
Give a slide a blocks[] list and blocks.py renders its content into the
house components; a slide without one comes in as a titled placeholder.
Prefer blocks: the renderer refuses the markup that breaks a deck.
Keep the real plan next to the deck, in presentations/<slug>/_src/,
so the deck can be regenerated after an edit.
Every fact on a slide comes from the case-study pages, never from memory.
